The regular season is rapidly coming to an end, and the Boston Red Sox still don't have ace pitcher Garrett Crochet back. That could be changing soon, though.
It had previously been reported that Crochet was set to return for the first round of the playoffs. Now, Chris Cotillo of MassLive noted in a report that the Red Sox may be pushing to have Crochet pitch in the regular season. This would act as a kind of rehab outing.
"The comebacks of potential October contributors like Tanner Houck, Garrett Crochet, Johan Oviedo and others might also be aided by the fact the Red Sox might have a week (or more) to set up for the postseason," Cotillo wrote. "It's not out of the question that the club has someone like Crochet pitch in one of the final regular season games of the year in what's effectively a rehab outing at the major league level in a game that matters little in the standings."
After finishing second in AL Cy Young voting in 2025, 2026 has been a major disappointment for Crochet. He has a 6.30 ERA and hasn't pitched since April 29th, when he originally hit the IL with left shoulder inflammation. He would later also be diagnosed with a lat strain.
When Crochet does return, it won't be in the rotation. He doesn't have time to build up to that. Instead, the Red Sox are going to be using him out of the bullpen. he
Boston Red Sox Ace Garrett Crochet Doesn't Have Time for a Rehab
The reality for Garrett Crochet is that time is running out for a rehab assignment, and he likely won't have time to make one. That's why the Red Sox would likely want to bring him back before a playoff series.
Regardless of if that chance to come back before the postseason happens, however, Crochet is confident in himself.
"Someone brought it up the other day. They were like, isn't that crazy? I'm like, not really," Crochet said on Monday. "I mean, not [to be all] me, me, me, me, but I've done crazy things before. I'm not Joe Schmoe. I've done impressive things. I think that that would be a big ask for some people, but I don't think it's a crazy ask for me."
This isn't entirely new territory for Crochet. In 2020, the Chicago White Sox added him to their postseason roster when he had limited time in live action due to the pandemic and coming out of college. He pitched well in that brief opportunity, throwing 0.2 innings with 2 strikeouts.
The Red Sox Postseason Rotation is Up for Debate
Heading into the postseason, pitching is a strength for the Red Sox. Even with injuries, that much has become obvious. Still, questions remain about the actual rotation in the postseason.
Sonny Gray and Payton Tolle will make starts in a three-game series. That's not up for debate. There is debate about which of the two gets Game One. Then, Game Three is going to be between Ranger Suarez and Jake Bennett. The lean there is certainly for the well-paid Suarez, who is a veteran with postseason success. However, stranger things have happened.
Starters who could be coming back from injury, including Houck and Crochet, are going to be seen as relievers. That's presumably how the Red Sox will also continue to use Brayan Bello and Patrick Sandoval.

The Boston Red Sox haven't officially clinched a postseason spot, but all signs point toward a Wild Card Series rematch at Yankee Stadium.
Pitching depth was a problem for the Red Sox in last year's playoff meeting with the Yankees. Their ace Garrett Crochet propelled them to victory in Game 1, but Brayan Bello and an inexperienced Connelly Early couldn't get the job done in Games 2 and 3.
This time, Boston's pitching will be a strength. Veteran right-hander Sonny Gray, rookie southpaw Payton Tolle, and veteran lefty Ranger Suarez can go toe-to-toe with most clubs' 1-through-3. The question is, what's the optimal order to put them in for the three-game Wild Card Series?
It's a good problem to have, and there's really no wrong answer. That said, here's our ideal Wild Card Series rotation for Boston as it looks to avenge last year's crushing defeat:
Justin Leger
Game 1: Sonny Gray
Gray isn't the "sexy" pick. That would be the mustached man I have starting Game 2.
But in what's sure to be an electrifying environment at Yankee Stadium, I want a dependable veteran on the mound to begin the series. I want Mr. Consistency.
All season long, Gray has fit that description.
Gray has a 17-5 record (tied for MLB lead in wins) with a 2.76 ERA through 27 starts. Since Crochet went down with an early-season injury, the 36-year-old has stepped up as the Red Sox' de facto ace with 18 quality starts (tied for seventh in MLB).
Unlike Tolle, Gray has plenty of experience pitching at Yankee Stadium. He's had his fair share of rough starts there throughout his 14-year career, especially during his brief stint with New York, but he was solid there earlier this season with three earned runs across 6.1 innings pitched in a 5-3 victory. In his other start against the Yankees at Fenway Park, he took a no-hitter into the eighth inning.
It'll be an uphill battle for the Red Sox regardless of who's on the mound, because Cy Young frontrunner Cam Schlittler will be poised to shut down Boston's bats yet again. Still, Gray can be counted on to give the Sox a chance to win, and if they lose, they'll have great options to lean on in Games 2 and 3.
Game 2: Payton Tolle
If Tolle is named the Red Sox' Game 1 starter, I won't complain. I'd be slightly concerned that his 0.1 IP in last year's Wild Card Series marks his only experience pitching at Yankee Stadium, but that isn't worth panicking about. He seems built for the bright lights.
Tolle looked sharp in both of his starts against the Yankees at Fenway this season. During his first outing in April, the 23-year-old allowed just one run on three hits across six innings. In his second start against them in June, he carried a perfect game into the sixth inning, finishing with no runs and just one hit allowed over seven innings pitched.
Those were two of many outings this season in which Tolle has looked like an ace. He'll have to perform like one throughout Boston's postseason run, and if he gets the ball in Game 2, he might be counted on to keep Boston's season alive.
Game 3: Ranger Suarez
If it comes down to a do-or-die Game 3, I feel great about Ranger Suarez taking the mound. The 31-year-old veteran has the postseason pedigree with an impressive 1.48 ERA in 11 career appearances (eight starts) with the Philadelphia Phillies.
Suarez endured a second-half slump but has looked more like himself in his last two outings. After tossing seven shutout innings against the Baltimore Orioles on Sept. 4, he allowed just one run across seven innings while striking out eight Kansas City Royals hitters on Saturday. This is the version of Suarez the Red Sox expected to get when they signed him to a five-year, $130 million contract in the offseason.
If Suarez struggles, the Red Sox will have the luxury of an elite bullpen to lean on. Brayan Bello has been an excellent bulk option since reverting to a relief role. Jake Bennett could be a legitimate weapon out of the 'pen as well, along with Crochet if he returns in time from his injury.
Mitchael Hurley
Game 1: Payton Tolle
I'm not opposed to statistics influencing baseball decisions. I rely on statistics more than I should.
But in this case, I don't think they matter. If you've watched the Red Sox this year, it could not be more clear that Payton Tolle is very much the heart and soul of this team. And the idea of sending him out onto the mound at Yankee Stadium with the whole baseball world watching just feels like the obvious choice.
If the Red Sox are going to win a series like this one, they're going to need to be the team with more energy. Nobody would bring more juice to the mound than Tolle. If he can step onto the field on a rainy Sunday four hours after first pitch was scheduled and instantly deliver an immaculate inning in the first, it's frightening to think what type of energy he can bring to a Game 1 start.
The Yankees have struggled against him this year, but even if they hadn't, I've gotta send Tolle to the mound for Game 1.
Game 2: Sonny Gray
In another year, in another circumstance, the 36-year-old Sonny Gray would be in line to win his first career Cy Young Award.
Of course, Cam Schlittler, the Yankees' presumed Game 1 starter, has wrecked any and all Cy Young debate with his sterling season in New York. Still, Gray is having one of the best seasons of his 14-year career, and he has to pitch in this series.
He did allow a pair of homers in his lone start at Yankee Stadium this season, and he's given up 22 homers in 23 appearances there in his career. With the short porch looming and the crowd always looking to erupt, that would be my concern.
But Gray's been great all year, he's been great down the stretch, and the Red Sox will ensure that he's properly rested for this one.
Game 3: Ranger Suarez
Would it look bad if the Red Sox potentially lost the series in two games and never sent Ranger Suarez and his 1.48 postseason ERA to the mound? It sure would.
But given the years that Tolle and Gray have had, I think the Red Sox could live with it.
There is some concern that he got rocked in the Bronx on Aug. 30 (six earned runs in 5.1 innings), but he also allowed one run in six innings in his first start at Yankee Stadium earlier in the season.
Considering the Red Sox had to send rookie Connelly Early out there in Game 3 a year ago to make his fifth career start, the team is clearly in a much better position if another Game 3 awaits them in the Bronx.

ARLINGTON -- Tanner Houck continued his rehab assignment with his third Minor League appearance on Tuesday, while Garrett Crochet threw another bullpen session at Fenway Park as both worked toward returning to Boston in relief roles.
The right-hander entered in the seventh and struck out Oliver Dunn looking at a 94.1 mph fastball. He then walked a batter before getting Austin Slater to swing through a 93.6 mph four-seamer and Jack Suwinski to chase an 83.5 mph sweeper.
Houck threw 22 pitches (11 strikes) and reached 94.2 mph with his fastball.
The 30-year-old is expected to make his next appearance on Friday, when he is scheduled for a longer outing in the 45-, 50-pitch range.
“Obviously some swing and miss in there. He has that capability,” interim manager Chad Tracy said ahead of Boston's bout with the Rangers Wednesday. “We all know -- and he said [it] himself, each time he touches the mound, getting his rhythm -- he gets a little bit more comfortable. That's all part of it. The strike-throwing piece and getting command of your pitches.
“So it seems at this point he's at least taking a step forward each time he goes out there, which is good. This next one will be good, being able to see [if he can] replicate that over a longer stretch of pitches.”
Crochet also took another step in his recovery.
The 2025 American League Cy Young Award runner-up threw a 30-pitch bullpen session at Fenway Park. Tracy said the session went well, but as of Wednesday the team did not have much clarity on Crochet’s next steps. He will continue his throwing program this week before the Red Sox re-evaluate him over the weekend.
Crochet has been building up his workload and intensity in recent bullpen sessions. He threw 25 pitches in his previous session Friday, when he incorporated his sweeper and threw his fastball in the 92-93 mph range.

Back in April, the Boston Red Sox's season was going off the rails.
The Red Sox started the season off with a 10-17 record and opted to fire a World Series-winning manager in Alex Cora — plus a handful of other coaches — and take a gamble by turning the reins over to interim manager Chad Tracy. At the time, it seemed like the sky was falling. That's because the losses kept piling up, so much so that the Red Sox were 14 games below .500 at 32-46 on June 25.
At the time, the season looked like a disaster. The Red Sox were trending towards being sellers ahead of the trade deadline, both Roman Anthony and Garrett Crochet were on the Injured List with no end in sight, and it seemed like chief baseball officer Craig Breslow's seat was getting hotter and hotter. But the Red Sox transformed their season and now, with the season winding down, ESPN's Buster Olney reported on Wednesday that the expectation is that both Breslow and Tracy will stay on with Boston beyond the 2026 season.
"But Breslow's vision of a team succeeding with pitching and defense fully manifested, and the Red Sox are closing in on a playoff berth and will likely face the Yankees in the wild-card round, again," Olney wrote. "Manager Chad Tracy has been working under an interim tag all season, something of a head-scratcher; it may be that the two sides talked about the idea of an extension in midseason but set aside the topic for the offseason. But Boston is now expected to retain both Breslow and Tracy."
The Red Sox Are Making The Right Call
This is undoubtedly the right call for the Red Sox at this time.
Let's start with Breslow. Whether you love him or not, he has built a team that can go on a run. Sure, there have been some misses over the last few years. Losing Alex Bregman was a public relations disaster. Not landing one of the big free agent bats, including Kyle Schwarber and Pete Alonso, this past offseason also was a surprise. But there are far more wins under Breslow's belt, than losses.
Sonny Gray is going to get Cy Young Award votes and has been Boston's ace this season. Ranger Suárez was an All-Star. Willson Contreras was an All-Star. Caleb Durbin is the heart and the soul of the 2026 Red Sox. Now, the Red Sox have an All-Star catcher on their hands in Adley Rutschman. Bringing back Mickey Gasper has turned into a game-changing move. And the list goes on. The Red Sox have a roster that can make noise.
On the Tracy front, there was obviously a learning curve to being a big league manager taking over during a season, especially in such a high-profile market, like Boston. He has handled the role with grace and has clearly gotten better as the year has gone on. Plus, it doesn't hurt that the Red Sox went on a historic 15-game winning streak and put together one of the best mid-season turnarounds in MLB history. All in all, these two should both be back in 2026 and it sounds like that will be the reality.

item.content:encoded:
Postseason baseball is right around the corner, which means it’s time to analyze a certain starting pitcher who seems to have American League Cy Young honors pretty much wrapped up with a bow.
I’m talking about New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler, who’s in the midst of an incredibly successful second season in the majors and looks like he’ll be a force in the league for a long time.
After former Detroit Tigers star Tarik Skubal walked away with the American League Cy Young in both 2024 and 2025, Schlittler is looking to assert himself as the new frontline pitcher in the American League. Let’s just say if Skubal didn’t get traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers and still remained on the Detroit Tigers, Schlittler probably still would have the upper hand, which is pretty impressive.
Other elite arms like Dylan Cease, Parker Messick, Drew Rasmussen and Reid Detmers have certainly given him a run for his money, but Schlittler is likely to take home the hardware when it’s all said and done.
He is also looking to be the Yankees’ second Cy Young Award winner in the last four years. Gerrit Cole took home the honors in 2023 after his excellent campaign, in which he owned a 2.63 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Schlittler’s 2026 campaign has actually been even better.
Now that everything has been set up, it’s time to dig deeper into what has fueled Schlittler’s elite 2026 campaign.
*Stats pulled from games completed through September 14.
Schlittler Came Out of the Blue, Kind Of
Up until the 2025 season, most people probably didn’t even know who Cam Schlittler was and what organization he was a part of. He was drafted by the Yankees in the seventh round of the 2022 draft out of Northeastern University.
He was an all-around solid pitcher in college over his three seasons, posting a 2.62 ERA and 1.08 WHIP, with 30 out of his 31 appearances being starts.
Schlittler didn’t make his affiliated debut within the Yankees system until the 2023 season and showed mixed results between rookie ball, Single-A, and High-A.
Even though he struck out a lot of batters and kept home runs to a minimum, he issued a lot of walks, which inflated his surface numbers.
Over the next two years spanning the 2024 and 2025 seasons, he gradually made his way through the Yankees’ minor league system and started to show some solid improvements.
By the time the 2025 campaign rolled around, Schlittler found himself on MLB Pipeline’s list of the Yankees’ top 30 prospects for the first time, being slotted in at number 12.
He was mowing down hitters, limiting walks, limiting home runs and was simply putting it all together between Double-A and Triple-A.
| Season | HR/9 | BB/9 | K/9 |
| 2023 | 0.8 | 4.1 | 9.8 |
| 2024 | 0.7 | 4.1 | 11.5 |
| 2025 | 0.5 | 3.1 | 11.6 |
Schlittler’s excellent performance was evident to the Yankees front office, and the organization decided it was time to give him a shot at the major league level. Let’s just say it’s been stunning to see what he’s been able to accomplish so quickly.
Pure Dominance in the Majors
Now that I’ve highlighted Schlittler’s underlooked journey to the big leagues, hopefully you’ll appreciate his insane numbers a little more and notice how far he has come along in terms of development.
He had a nice cup of tea with the Yankees in 2025 after he debuted on July 9, finishing the season with an excellent 2.96 ERA and 1.22 WHIP spanning a stretch of 14 starts. A majority of his growth in the minor leagues had carried over to the majors, which was really encouraging to see.
Last year, Schlittler gave us a little glimpse into what he’d provide long term, but no one realized what kind of pitching monster he’d turn into presently in 2026.
You could even argue that he’s been better than Jacob Misiorowski because their numbers have pretty much been identical, give or take. That means you could argue he’s the best pitcher in the majors currently.
So far in 2026, across 31 starts and 184.2 innings pitched, Schlittler has shown pure dominance, pitching to a superb 1.95 ERA and 0.90 WHIP. His ratios have been really good, as backed up by his excellent 6 H/9, 0.8 HR/9, 2.1 BB/9 and 11.1 K/9.
Schlittler currently leads the American League with 5.9 fWAR. He ranks second overall, only trailing Misirowski, who has been worth 6.0 fWAR.
His underlying peripherals look great, including his 2.87 xERA and 2.57 FIP. That is a result of his ability to limit dangerous contact and total baserunners via low hit and walk rates, as previously mentioned.
In terms of pitching run value calculated by Baseball Savant, Schlittler ranks fourth in the majors, currently worth +38 runs. He trails only Yoshinobu Yamamoto (39), Dylan Cease (39) and Jacob Misiorowski (47).
The reason as to why his pitching run value is so high is because of how effective his pitch arsenal has been. Schlittler primarily works with four quality pitches: a four-seam fastball (44%), cutter (25%), sinker (20%) and curveball (10%).
The fastball combo of his four-seam and sinker has been lethal and goes to show how important and effective tunneling can be.
Schlittler’s fastball, which averages 98 mph, is worth a +27 run value, and batters have only managed a .164 batting average and .230 wOBA against the offering. His counterpart 97.8 mph sinker is being valued at a +11 run value, with a .172 batting average and .266 xwOBA.
Also note that Schlittler has 6.8 feet of extension, which places him in the 81st percentile. This helps create a faster perceived velocity for an already powerful fastball mix.
His cutter, which averages 94.7 mph, has been a hint above average with a +1 run value, while his 86.3 mph curveball has been his worst and least-used pitch, worth -1 in run value. If Schlittler can improve just one of those pitches, it could be wraps for his opponents.
Schlittler’s stuff has been very good, to say the least, and batters are having a really hard time making contact on his offerings. His current 34.2% chase rate ranks in the 85th percentile, while his 29.1% whiff rate ranks in the 79th percentile.
Despite the fact that opponents are making limited contact with Schlittler’s offerings, they still have managed to make decent contact when they do connect.
This is one of the few flaws in Schlittler’s already great profile that could use some improvement. Opponents have managed a 7.7% barrel rate (45th percentile) and 39.1% hard-hit (44th percentile) rate against him. Those numbers aren’t bad, but they could be better.
Will Schlittler Take Home AL Cy Young Honors?
Plain and simple, Schlittler has been dominant. And there’s actually a good chance he gets even better down the road based on what we’ve looked at.
It seems very likely that Schlittler will be named the 2026 American League Cy Young when it’s all said and done. Cease has pleaded his case in the best way he’s able to, but all signs are pointing to Schlittler.
Simply just looking at Schlittler’s and Cease’s second-half splits pretty much ends the conversation.
Yordan Alvarez seems like the leading candidate for American League Most Valuable Player, but you’d think Schlittler will be considered there as well. Alvarez leads all AL batters with 5.8 fWAR, but Schlittler does have him topped with 5.9 fWAR — something to keep an eye out for.
We’ll have to wait and see what happens, but Schlittler looks to have wrapped up the conversation for the American League Cy Young.

When the Boston Red Sox made some additions to their starting rotation last winter, they were hoping to rebuild it around ace Garrett Crochet. Little did they know that making those moves would turn out to be monster moves.
After losing out on Alex Bregman in free agency to the Chicago Cubs, Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow pivoted to pitching. He signed left-hander Ranger Suárez of the Philadelphia Phillies. Earlier in the offseason, Breslow acquired veteran Sonny Gray from the St. Louis Cardinals.
That is turning into the biggest offseason addition made by Boston. He is going to finish at least in the top 5 in the American League Cy Young voting, but will be a free agent following the season with an option for 2027. Breslow and Gray will have a decision to make this winter, according to Kerry Miller of Bleacher Report.
Boston Red Sox Facing Sonny Gray Decision This Winter
When decisions are to be made for 2027, Gray has a mutual option of $30 million. Now, whether or not Gray plays next season remains to be seen, according to Alex Speier of the Boston Globe.
“If my family wants me to hang it up, I’ll be done in a heartbeat,” Gray said, per Speier.
If they don’t want him to retire, the Red Sox would love to have him back. He is 17-5 in his first season in Boston with a 2.76 ERA in 27 starts. He has been a workhorse in 156.2 innings with 140 strikeouts. Gray has struggled in recent outings. However, he is still on track to get the ball in Game 1 of the AL wild-card series.
“Even with major money committed to Ranger Suárez and Garrett Crochet in the rotation already, chief baseball officer Craig Breslow will probably pick up the team’s half of the option,” Miller wrote.
“The question is whether Gray will. Considering he’ll pitch next season at 37, he’s probably not going to get more than $30 million for 2027 as a free agent. However, if he declines the option, the Red Sox will owe him a $10 million buyout. So he could collect that buyout, try to get at least $20 million for 2027, and perhaps pursue a multi-year commitment. He has plenty to consider.”
Crochet has been out injured for a majority of this season and is looking for a postseason return. Suárez has been better in his last couple of starts in September.
Boston Red Sox Facing Key Offseason Decision
Gray is scheduled to make his next start on Thursday night against the Texas Rangers in Arlington. Then he’ll get one more next week before his start in the wild-card round. Depending on how far the Red Sox go, all eyes could turn to 2027.
Boston’s rotation next season, if healthy when the season begins, with Gray, could be one of the top ones in the American League. If there is any question as to whether or not Gray has another year left in him, that should have been answered by his 2026 season.
There are some big decisions coming for Breslow this winter. Gray is going to be at the top of that list.

Dylan Cease's first season with the Toronto Blue Jays has been tremendous. He rewarded the front office's confidence after signing a lucrative contract this offseason.
Every team needs an ace. Cease assumed that role and took off with it. In the middle of a tight playoff race, the Blue Jays feel comfortable when the 30-year-old takes the mound. Since the All-Star break, Toronto is 7-4 when Cease pitches.
He's accomplished a lot of firsts this season, but could he add one more to the list?
Can Cease Win His First Cy Young?
Cease has been a strikeout machine since entering the league. He's eclipsed 200+ strikeouts for six consecutive seasons, and this year, he has a new career-high of 236 strikeouts and counting.
Now, Cease has his eyes set on his first American League Cy Young Award. In 2022, he was the runner-up to Justin Verlander, who won the award unanimously. In 2024, Cease finished fourth behind Paul Skenes (3), Zack Wheeler (2), and Chris Sale (1).
This could be his best chance yet. Jared Greenspan of MLB.com laid out the latest A.L. Cy Young poll. Cease finished second behind New York Yankees pitcher Cam Schlittler. Cease received 126 points and Schlittler received 160 points.
Comparing Cease and Schlittler
Schlittler: 14-6, 184.2 IP, 1.95 ERA, 0.90 WHIP, 228 SO, 44 BB
Cease: 11-5, 166.1 IP, 2.38 ERA, 1.06 WHIP, 236 SO, 72 BB
While this may be Cease's best chance, those statistics suggest it will be tough to defeat Schlittler. The righty would have to put up incredible numbers over his final three or four starts, and Schlittler would need to go in the opposite direction.
The majority of Cease's advanced metrics rank in the 90th percentile or higher on Baseball Savant. His average exit velocity (85.6), whiff percentage (33.4), strikeout percentage (35.3), and hard-hit percentage (31.9) are some of the best in baseball this year.
Cease became the first Blue Jays pitcher to start the All-Star Game since Roy Halladay in 2009. It's incredible to think this was Cease's first All-Star nod. He would become the first Toronto pitcher to win the Cy Young Award. Two have won the award this century (Robbie Ray, 2021, and Roy Halladay, 2009).
Regardless of what happens, no one can take away the brilliant year Cease has had. The talent was always there. It was about finding the right organization to unlock it. The Blue Jays became the place where Cease could thrive.
Zion Trammell graduated from TCU in 2023 with a degree in sports broadcasting and journalism. He currently writes for TCU Horned Frogs on SI. In addition to writing, he is the play-by-play voice for Southlake Carroll baseball and hosts a TCU show on the Bleav Network.

item.content:encoded:
2026 정규시즌이 단 2주만을 남겨둔 가운데, 아메리칸리그와 내셔널리그 사이영상 수상 레이스가 사실상 막을 내린 것처럼 보입니다.
이는 양 리그 모두 쟁쟁한 후보들이 포진해 있는 다른 후보군 때문이라기보다는 독보적인 선두 주자들 때문입니다. 뉴욕 양키스의 캠 슐리틀러와 밀워키 브루어스의 제이콥 미시오로스키가 확실하게 쐐기를 박았습니다. 올해 마지막 사이영상 모의 투표에 참여한 MLB.com 투표인단 32명은 두 명의 강력한 강속구 투수를 각 리그의 만장일치 1위로 선정했습니다.
전문가들은 지금까지의 결과뿐만 아니라 남은 2주 동안의 판도가 어떻게 전개될지 예상하여 트로피를 거머쥘 주인공에게 투표했습니다. 투표인단은 각 리그에서 상위 5명의 선수를 선정하도록 요청받았으며, 투수들은 5-4-3-2-1 점수 스케일(1위 표 5점, 2위 표 4점 등)에 따라 점수를 획득했습니다.
별도 표기가 없는 한 모든 기록은 13일(미국 현지시간) 경기 기준이었습니다.
아메리칸리그
1. 캠 슐리틀러, 뉴욕 양키스 (총 160점; 1위 표 32장)
슐리틀러는 13일 서브웨이 시리즈 최종전에서 뉴욕 메츠 타선을 상대로 6이닝 동안 무실점 피칭을 선보이며 시즌 평균자책점을 1.95로 낮췄습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그에서 가장 뛰어난 기록일 뿐만 아니라, 메이저리그 규정 이닝 충족 투수 중 미시오로스키와 공동으로 가장 낮은 기록이기도 합니다. 슐리틀러는 최근 7경기 연속으로 1실점 이하 경기만을 기록하며 자신의 메이저리그 첫 풀타임 시즌을 화려하게 마무리하고 있습니다. 그는 지난 포스트시즌 아메리칸리그 와일드카드 시리즈에서 센세이션을 일으켰던 바로 그 공식인 '삼진아웃을 유도하는 세 가지 패스트볼 조합'으로 타자들을 계속해서 압도하고 있습니다. 10월 가을야구가 다가오는 가운데, 그의 화려한 앙코르 무대가 코앞으로 다가왔습니다.
2. 딜런 시즈, 토론토 블루제이스 (126점)
시즈는 지난해 11월 토론토 블루제이스와 체결한 7년 계약의 첫해부터 완벽 그 자체인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 그는 가장 최근 경기인 13일 볼티모어 오리올스전에서 9개의 삼진을 솎아내며, 올 시즌 9개 이상의 탈삼진을 기록한 경기를 13차례로 늘렸습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그 어떤 투수보다도 많은 기록입니다. 시즈의 통산 236개의 탈삼진은 개인 단일시즌 최다 기록 경신이자 메이저리그 전체에서 미시오로스키와 함께 공동 1위에 해당합니다. 올해 시즈는 치명적인 포심 패스트볼/슬라이더 조합에 더 균형 잡힌 구종 배합을 더해 상대 타선을 공략하는 다양한 방식을 구사하고 있습니다. 이것이 바로 시즈의 피안타율(.177)이 아메리칸리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 가장 낮은 이유 중 일부입니다.
3. 파커 메식, 클리블랜드 가디언스 (77점)
슐리틀러나 시즈와 같은 반열은 아닐지 몰라도, 메식은 루키 시즌에 부정할 수 없는 환상적인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 개성 있는 폼을 지닌 이 좌완 투수는 11일 미네소타 트윈스를 상대로 한 직전 등판에서 5.1이닝 동안 단 1실점만을 허용했으며, 치열한 페넌트레이스 혈전 속에서도 그것이 바로 메식이 해내는 방식입니다. 이번 시즌 5이닝 이상을 소화하면서 1실점 이하만 내준 경기가 슐리틀러와 시즈보다 많은 아메리칸리그 투수는 단 두 명뿐입니다. 메식의 2.51의 평균자책점은 메이저리그 전체 5위에 해당하는 기록입니다. 그의 성공 비결은 바로 포심 패스트볼입니다. 메식은 구속이 시속 94.3마일(약 151.8km)로 아주 빠르지는 않지만, 스타캐스트의 득점 가치(run value) 지표에 따르면 그의 포심은 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 개별 구종 중 하나로 꼽힙니다.
4. 드류 라스무센, 탬파베이 레이스 (52점)
금요일, 탬파베이는 주니어 카미네로의 극적인 끝내기 홈런에 힘입어 올 시즌 구단 중 가장 먼저 포스트시즌 진출을 확정 지었습니다. 잊지 말아야 할 점은 라스무센이 그날 탬파베이의 선발 투수로 등판해 1실점 투구로 7이닝을 가볍게 책임졌다는 사실입니다. 탬파베이가 승리한 것은 놀라운 일이 아닙니다. 그것이 바로 라스무센이 마운드에 올랐을 때 그들이 보여주는 방식이기 때문입니다. 탬파베이는 올스타 브레이크 이전부터 거슬러 올라가 그의 최근 선발 등판 10경기를 모두 승리로 장식했습니다. 31세의 우완 투수인 그는 세 가지 형태의 패스트볼 구종과 완벽한 제구력을 바탕으로 아메리칸리그 평균자책점(2.81), WHIP(0.92), 피안타율(.203) 부문에서 모두 상위 5위 이내에 이름을 올리고 있습니다.
5. 소니 그레이, 보스턴 레드삭스 (37점)
보스턴은 야구계 최고 수준의 투수진을 앞세워 포스트시즌 진출을 향해 순항하고 있습니다. 이 문장은 개막전 당시였다면 당연히 이해되었겠지만, 좌완 투수 개럿 크로셰가 4월 말 이후 부상으로 전력에서 이탈했다는 사실을 안다면 이야기가 다릅니다. 크로셰의 공백 속에서 그레이가 에이스 역할을 톡톡히 해냈습니다. 그는 27경기에 선발 등판해 17승 5패 평균자책점 2.76을 기록 중이며, 투수 승리 기록이 전부를 말해주는 것은 아니지만 아메리칸리그에서 그레이보다 더 많은 승리를 거둔 투수가 없다는 점은 주목할 만합니다. 그는 통산 세 번째 아메리칸리그 사이영상 투표 상위 5위 진입을 노리고 있습니다. 2023년 미네소타 소속으로 투표 2위를 차지했으며, 2015년에는 오클랜드 소속으로 3위에 오른 바 있습니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 리드 데트머스(LA 에인절스), 개빈 윌리엄스(클리블랜드 가디언스), 닉 마르티네즈(탬파베이 레이스), 마이클 와카(캔자스시티 로열스)
내셔널리그
1. 제이콥 미시오로스키, 밀워키 브루어스 (총 160점, 1위 표 32장)
'더 미즈'는 지난 8일 시카고 컵스를 상대로 6.1이닝 동안 탈삼진 9개를 솎아내며 단 1실점만 내주는 센세이션한 투구로 보기 드문 부진을 말끔히 씻어냈습니다. 압도적인 구위를 자랑하는 이 우완 투수는 평균자책점(1.95), 피안타율(.155), 탈삼진(236개)을 포함하여 거의 모든 주요 투수 통계 부문에서 내셔널리그 선두를 달리고 있습니다. 161.1이닝을 소화한 지금까지도 미시오로스키는 여전히 강력한 불을 뿜어내고 있습니다. 그는 이번 시즌 시속 100마일 이상의 공을 무려 1,010개나 던졌으며, 이는 이 부문 2위인 투수(메이슨 밀러, 468개)의 두 배를 훌쩍 뛰어넘는 수치입니다.
2. 크리스 세일, 애틀랜타 브레이브스 (106점)
나이를 가늠할 수 없는 이 불세출의 투수는 시즌 막판 내셔널리그 사이영상 레이스의 격차를 좁히기 위해 최선의 노력을 다하고 있습니다. 세일의 평균자책점 2.18은 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 좋은 기록이자, 37세의 이 베테랑이 2018년 이후 단일 시즌 기준 기록한 가장 낮은 수치입니다. 그는 최근 23경기 연속으로 3실점 이하 경기만을 치르며 놀라울 정도로 꾸준한 모습을 보여주었습니다. 이번 시즌 16경기 이상 연속으로 3실점 이하를 기록한 선발 투수는 그 외에 단 한 명도 없습니다. 세일은 향상된 구속 덕분에 세월을 역행하고 있으며, 선발 투수로 활약한 통산 그 어느 때보다 더 빠른 공을 뿌리고 있습니다.
3. 크리스토퍼 산체스, 필라델피아 필리스 (99점)
산체스는 최근 두 경기에서 총 9실점을 허용하며 이전 모의 투표보다 한 계단 내려앉았습니다. 하지만 이 마른 좌완 투수는 여전히 사이영상 후보로 손색이 없는 시즌을 만들어가고 있습니다. 산체스는 메이저리그 전체에서 두 번째로 많은 이닝(187.1이닝)을 소화했으며, 내셔널리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 5번째로 좋은 평균자책점(2.79)과 3번째로 좋은 FIP(수비 무관 평균자책점, 2.72)를 기록 중입니다. 야구 통계 전문 사이트 베이스볼레퍼런스(Baseball Reference) 기준 WAR에 따르면, 산체스는 7.6의 WAR을 기록하며 2026년 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 투수로 자리매김했습니다.
4. 헤수스 루자르도, 필라델피아 필리스 (52점)
루자르도는 노동절에 내셔널리그 동부지구 선두인 애틀랜타를 상대로 거둔 눈부신 완봉승에 힘입어 최종 사이영상 모의 투표 명단에 이름을 올렸습니다. 이 좌완 투수가 마땅히 받아야 할 찬사를 받는 시점은 이미 한참 지났습니다. 루자르도는 최근 12경기에서 8승 1패 평균자책점 1.66을 기록하며, 7월 1일 이후 메이저리그 전체에서 가장 낮은 평균자책점을 마크했고 8월 내셔널리그 이달의 투수로 선정되었습니다. 지난 시즌 연마한 치명적인 스위퍼를 무기로 장착한 루자르도는 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 높은 탈삼진율(30.4%)을 기록하고 있습니다. 필리스 팬들은 루자르도가 어깨 통증으로 인해 직전 등판을 건너뛰어 가슴을 졸였으나, MRI 검사 후 본인은 "걱정하지 않는다"고 안심시켰습니다.
5. 야마모토 요시노부, LA 다저스 (43점)
우리는 이제 야마모토에게 너무나 많은 것을 기대한 나머지, 지난 9일 레즈전에서 보여준 7이닝 10탈삼진 역투 같은 최고의 피칭조차 당연하게 느껴질 정도입니다. 그는 여전히 할리우드(LA)에 어울리는 화려한 스타 군단 선발진의 에이스로서 26경기에 등판해 평균자책점 2.62를 기록하고 있습니다. 미시오로스키에 이어 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 낮은 0.88의 WHIP과 .184의 피안타율을 기록 중인 야마모토만큼 주자 출루를 철저히 억제하는 투수는 드뭅니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 체이스 번스(신시내티 레즈), 에두아르도 로드리게스(애리조나 다이아몬드백스), 메이슨 밀러(샌디에이고 파드리스), 잭 휠러(필라델피아 필리스)

MLB award predictions 2026: MVPs Ohtani and Judge will be dethroned
The 2026 Major League Baseball season has less than two weeks to go, and most of league's major awards have runaway favorites – with new faces expected to win the MVP and Cy Young honors in each league.
The Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong will certainly dethrone Shohei Ohtani for the NL MVP award, snapping Ohtani's three-year reign that dates back to his final season with the Los Angeles Angels. In the AL, the Houston Astros' Yordan Alvarez is in the running for the Triple Crown and should win the award over the Tampa Ray Rays' Junior Caminero, with back-to-back winner Aaron Judge hampered by an injury this season.
Both expected Cy Young winners are in their second MLB seasons: Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees and Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers. Each right-hander sports an ERA below 2.00 entering Tuesday and have fans amped about the next generation of aces in MLB.
Here's our predictions for the 2026 MLB awards:
AL MVP: Yordan Alvarez, Astros
Triple Crown incoming? The 29-year-old has proven himself as one of the greatest sluggers of the era and should win this award easily, having already set a career-high with 38 home runs. He's the runaway favorite, but Houston getting back into the postseason would even further ice this for Alvarez.
Also in the running: Junior Caminero (Rays), Bobby Witt Jr. (Royals)
NL MVP: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs
With Shohei Ohtani injured this summer, PCA has locked this up as he closes in on the seventh 40-40 season in MLB history. The 24-year-old is putting together one of the greatest years ever, with a 9.3 fWAR while leading the National League in slugging and OPS.
Also in the running: Shohei Ohtani (Dodgers)
AL Cy Young: Cam Schlittler, Yankees
We knew Cam Schlittler was good after his impact as a rookie in 2025, but nobody could have fathomed the 25-year-old would be this good in his sophomore season. The right-hander is having one of the greatest pitching seasons could be the first Yankees pitcher with a sub-2 ERA since Ron Guidry in 1978. Even more impressive is his leading the AL in innings (184.2) and starts (31).
Also in the running: Dylan Cease (Blue Jays)
NL Cy Young: Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers
A controversial All-Star selection as a rookie last season, The Miz has been by far the NL's best pitcher at age 24, leading the league in ERA (1.95), strikeouts (236) and WHIP (0.80).
Also in the running: Chris Sale (Braves)
AL Rookie of the Year: Kevin McGonigle, Tigers
Things didn't go as planned for Tarik Skubal's final season in Detroit, but McGonigle's breakthrough is the major positive to take away from this year. The Tigers signed McGonigle to an eight-year, $150 million extension and the infielder who was 21 on opening day is currently approaching 7 WAR on the season.
Also in the running: Parker Messick (Guardians), Munetaka Murakami (White Sox)
NL Rookie of the Year: Sal Stewart, Reds
Stewart has been invaluable for the Reds, primarily playing the corner infield positions while also seeing time at second base, racking up 31 home runs with 107 RBIs and 15 steals.
Also in the running: JJ Wetherholt (Cardinals), Nolan McLean (Mets)

item.content:encoded:
Cam Schlittler brought his A-game on Sunday. Facing the Mets in the rubber game of the Subway Series at Yankee Stadium, the Yankees’ fireballer was nearly untouchable over the course of six scoreless innings, striking out eight while allowing just one hit, a fifth-inning double by Brett Baty. Meanwhile in Baltimore, the Blue Jays’ Dylan Cease worked around five walks to allow just one run over five innings while striking out nine. The two righties are engaged in an intriguing race for the AL Cy Young Award, one that could go down to the wire. The NL race is a tight one as well, with the Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski the favorite but hardly the only one under consideration.
The 25-year-old Schlittler and 24-year-old Misiorowski are undeniably the frontrunners in their respective leagues, from both statistical and narrative standpoints. They lead in our Tom Tango-modeled Cy Young projections, and as of mid-August, they dominated polls taken by MLB.com. Nonetheless, the statistical races that can influence both our perceptions and voter behavior aren’t entirely decided, and with less than two weeks to go in the regular season, the races are worth a closer look.
The 6-foot-7 Misiorowski and 6-foot-6 Schlittler share similarities beyond their impressive heights. Both are in their first full major league seasons, after arriving in mid-2025 and helping their teams to the playoffs while showing poise beyond their years; this October, they’ll be seasoned postseason veterans. They’re the majors’ two hardest-throwing starters, with Misiorowski breaking velocity records all over the place. His average four-seam velocity — a mind-blowing 100.6 mph — not only leads the majors, but it’s also the fastest single-season velocity by a starter in the pitch-tracking era (from 2008 onward), hardly surprising given that he owns the (scrolling, scrolling, scrolling) 117 fastest pitches by a starter in pitch-tracking history — including a record-setting 105.5-mph heater to the Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong on June 26 — and 353 of the 394 pitches of at least 102 mph thrown by a starter. Hunter Greene is the only other one in double digits (12). Schlittler merely ranks second among all starters this year, with an average velocity of 98.0 mph, which is still good for fifth in the pitch-tracking era.
Both righties have other exceptional offerings that test the adage “man cannot live by fastball alone,” in that Misiorowski’s cutter and Schlittler’s sinker are their second-most valuable pitches according to Statcast. But whatever they’re throwing, they’re dominating. Each leads his respective league in ERA (1.95 for both) and fWAR (6.0 for Misiorowski, 5.9 for Schlittler), with the Yankee additionally leading the AL in starts (31), innings (184 2/3), strikeout-walk differential (25.5%), and bWAR (7.1), and the Brewer leading the NL in strikeouts (236), strikeout rate (38.3%), and FIP (2.24). That ought to be enough to hand out the hardware, right?
Quite possibly, but not all of those statistical leads is insurmountable. Zooming in for a closer look first at the AL, Schlittler and Cease have separated themselves from the pack more so than they have from each other:
| Pitcher | W | L | GS | IP | K% | BB% | K-BB% | HR/9 | ERA | xERA | FIP | fWAR | bWAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cam Schlittler | 14 | 6 | 31 | 184.2 | 31.6% | 6.1% | 25.5% | 0.78 | 1.95 | 2.88 | 2.57 | 5.9 | 7.1 |
| Dylan Cease | 11 | 5 | 28 | 166.1 | 35.3% | 10.8% | 24.6% | 0.60 | 2.38 | 2.81 | 2.48 | 5.6 | 6.0 |
| Parker Messick | 11 | 9 | 29 | 172.1 | 26.0% | 6.9% | 19.1% | 0.84 | 2.51 | 3.07 | 3.11 | 4.5 | 5.7 |
| Drew Rasmussen | 14 | 5 | 28 | 160.1 | 25.6% | 4.3% | 21.3% | 0.79 | 2.81 | 3.11 | 2.88 | 4.6 | 3.9 |
| Sonny Gray | 17 | 5 | 27 | 156.2 | 22.0% | 6.6% | 15.4% | 0.86 | 2.76 | 3.84 | 3.46 | 3.2 | 4.0 |
I couldn’t fit it in the table, but Schlittler is third in strikeouts (228) behind Cease (236) and Gavin Williams (235), whose run prevention numbers (3.78 ERA, 3.49 FIP) rule him out here. (Dan Szymborski has a closer look at Williams’ breakout up today.) Messick, Rasmussen, and Gray have all authored fine seasons, but none has a compelling enough statistical case to elevate him into the company of the top two; win totals and winning percentage don’t cut it these days. The ability of Schlittler and Cease to miss bats separates them in value from the rest of the group, both via our FIP-driven WAR and Baseball Reference’s version, where they don’t have to share as much credit (or blame) with their fielders given the lower rates of balls in play. More on that subject in a moment.
With Gerrit Cole scuffling late in his first season after returning from Tommy John surgery, and Max Fried limited to 18 starts by a bone bruise in his elbow, Schlittler has emerged as the Yankees’ bona fide ace and as one of the league’s true workhorses. Six other AL pitchers have made at least 30 starts so far, but only Michael Wacha has thrown at least 180 innings; he’s at 182 2/3, and while Tanner Bibee (177 1/3), Reid Detmers (174), Williams (174) and a couple others may get there, they won’t catch Schlittler. Nineteen of Schlittler’s starts have been quality starts, the league’s second-highest total behind Wacha (20); Cease is tied for eighth with 15. Schlittler has either put up zeroes or allowed just one run in 22 starts, including each of his last seven. Sixteen of those zero-or-one-run starts have lasted at least six innings; Gray and Rasmussen are among those tied for second with 13, while Cease is tied for sixth with 12. Beyond the aforementioned categories in which he’s led the league, Schlittler is second to Cease in FIP and xERA by less than one-tenth of a run, with the third-highest strikeout rate and sixth-lowest walk rate.
Cease, whom the Blue Jays signed to a seven-year, $210 million deal this past winter, has bounced back from an uneven 2025 performance with the Padres, one in which he put up a 4.54 ERA and a 3.56 FIP. He’s been every bit as good as the Blue Jays could have hoped for, something that can’t be said for many players on the defending AL champions. He has totaled seven starts of at least six innings with zero runs allowed, tied for third in the majors behind Cristopher Sánchez (10) and Rasmussen (eight); Schlittler is tied for seventh with six.
Cease has been the most unhittable starter in the AL, with the lowest batting average allowed (.177) and fewest hits per nine (5.68). He chalked up the first no-hitter of his career in 2024 while pitching for the Padres, and has flirted with a second one on a couple occasions this season. He tossed eight hitless innings on July 8 against the Giants at Oracle Park before allowing a single to Heliot Ramos to start the ninth, at which point he departed, having thrown 118 pitches in what was by then a 10-0 rout; days later, he was named to start the All-Star Game for the AL. He pitched 6 2/3 hitless innings against the Yankees on August 22 in the Bronx before allowing back-to-back singles to Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Austin Wells, and additionally threw a one-hit shutout against the Red Sox at Fenway Park on July 25, with a fifth-inning double by Andruw Monasterio the lone blemish.
Both Schlittler and Cease have averaged a hair under six innings per start (5.96 for the former, 5.94 for the latter). The difference in innings totals comes down to Cease’s having spent 15 days on the injured list for a mild hamstring strain starting in late May.
Cease has the higher strikeout rate, but also the higher walk rate — the highest among AL qualifiers, in fact — but even with that, his FIP and xERA are slightly better than Schlittler’s. Those estimators are defense-independent, but it’s worth noting the defenses behind the two pitchers. Statcast, which tracks the individual Fielding Run Values accumulated behind each pitcher, shows Cease with slightly more support, with his fielders putting up 7 FRV behind him compared to 5 FRV for Schlittler. The bWAR calculations, which start with actual runs allowed per nine innings with a variety of adjustments for defense, opposing offenses, and park factors, credit Cease with having the better defense behind him (based on team-level Defensive Runs Saved), worth 0.24 runs per nine to Schlittler’s 0.09 runs per nine. In other words, by that reckoning Cease shares more credit with his fielders, though that difference is canceled out by adjustments for his facing better offenses and pitching in a higher-scoring environment.
In the end, Schlittler’s combination of superior run prevention, better peripherals, and a larger innings load separates him from Cease by 1.1 bWAR and 0.3 fWAR. Depending upon where you fall on the spectrum of factoring in defense, it’s somewhere between a narrow margin and a substantial one, but either way it lines up with the consensus. Barring a blowup over his final couple of starts, Schlittler looks like the right call for the AL Cy Young.
The NL race isn’t as clear-cut:
| Pitcher | W | L | GS | IP | K% | BB% | K-BB% | HR/9 | ERA | xERA | FIP | fWAR | bWAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jacob Misiorowski | 14 | 5 | 27 | 161.1 | 38.3% | 6.7% | 31.7% | 0.78 | 1.95 | 2.10 | 2.24 | 6.0 | 5.6 |
| Cristopher Sánchez | 17 | 5 | 30 | 187.1 | 27.0% | 5.4% | 21.6% | 0.77 | 2.79 | 3.31 | 2.72 | 5.8 | 7.6 |
| Chris Sale | 14 | 9 | 26 | 157.0 | 30.3% | 4.9% | 25.4% | 0.52 | 2.18 | 3.05 | 2.29 | 5.7 | 5.5 |
| Jesús Luzardo | 14 | 5 | 29 | 178.2 | 29.4% | 8.8% | 20.7% | 0.76 | 2.87 | 2.85 | 2.78 | 5.5 | 6.4 |
On a pure rate basis, the numbers favor Misiorowski. Not only does he lead the NL in the half-dozen categories highlighted above, but he’s been even more unhittable than Cease, with a .155 batting average allowed and 4.91 hits per nine given up, both tops in the majors among qualifiers. But because he’s worked in a six-man rotation all season long, and has been kept on a slightly shorter leash — averaging 5.97 innings per start to Sale’s 6.04, Luzardo’s 6.14, and Sánchez’s 6.24 — he has thrown 26 fewer innings than Sánchez.
The results have generally been dazzling. Misiorowski has 10 starts with double-digit strikeout totals, second in the majors only to Williams; Cease has nine, Luzardo six, Sánchez five, Sale and Schlittler four. The Miz has six scoreless starts of at least six innings, including a 15-strikeout one-hit shutout against the Phillies on June 12, marred only by a fourth-inning Kyle Schwarber single. But even with a majors-leading 236 strikeouts, the innings total puts him at a slight disadvantage in some contexts. Misiorowski is tied for fifth in the league with 18 quality starts, with Sánchez tied for second (20) alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto, one behind Sandy Alcantara; Sale is fourth with 19, Luzardo tied for ninth with 17. Misiorowski’s total of 11 starts of at least six innings with no more than one run allowed trails Sánchez (13), as well as Luzardo and Sale (12 apiece).
Sánchez has the volume advantage. Working with a sinker that averages “only” 95.0 mph — offset by one of the game’s best changeups — he’s reached the 200-strikeout plateau for the second consecutive season; his 212 ranks third behind Misiorowski and Luzado (221). His strikeout rate ranks seventh, his walk rate third, his strikeout-walk differential fourth, behind Misiorowski, Sale, and Luzardo in that order. He made a huge impression earlier this season by reeling off a streak of 50 2/3 scoreless innings in May, the longest ever by a lefty, and the fifth longest of all time; not since Orel Hershiser’s 59-inning streak in 1988 broke Don Drysdale’s record had anyone reached 50. That streak helped Sánchez land the honor of starting the All-Star Game for the NL, though Misiorowski’s workload — he was scheduled to start on the Sunday before the game, officially ruling him out for the honor, and then was scratched from that outing due to arm fatigue — played a part. Even then, Sánchez’s 2.62 ERA was a full run per nine higher than Misiorowski’s. On that note, Sánchez has a 3.15 ERA and a 3.46 FIP since the break, though by FIP (2.70 before, 2.77 after), he’s been basically the same pitcher, and even his xERAs (3.24 before, 3.46 after) are closer than his actual ones.
The 37-year-old Sale has thrown even fewer innings than Misiorowski because he’s been given some extra rest between starts. It’s a choice that’s paid off handsomely for the Braves and for the pitcher, who cracked 100 mph on a pitch on August 27, his fastest since 2018, and who has been positively brilliant in the second half, with a 2.14 ERA and a 1.41 FIP, the latter thanks to a combination of a 32.6% strikeout rate, a 2.7% walk rate, and 0.15 homers per nine.
According to Statcast, Sale has gotten the best defensive support of this quartet at 5 FRV, ahead of Sánchez (3), Misiorowski (0), and Luzardo (-3). That defense has helped to offset Sale’s having an xERA almost a run higher than the Miz. The two are on nearly even footing in the grand scheme, but based on their performances to date, I don’t see anything that would elevate Sale past Misiorowski except some sentiment for the old guy, a likely future Hall of Famer.
As for Luzardo, there’s not much separating him from Sánchez. Though his season hasn’t been as eye-catching, it’s been stellar, but in the wake of his two-hit, 12-strikeout shutout against the Braves on September 7, he’s dealt with shoulder stiffness and inflammation. Thanks to a clean MRI, he’s avoided the injured list so far, though he did have a turn skipped, and it wouldn’t be surprising if his workload between here and October is dialed down.
The two Phillies have had to survive playing in front of the team’s notoriously lousy defense. Sánchez has the highest BABIP among NL qualifiers (.335), 41 points ahead of the seventh-ranked Luzardo (.294) and 101 points ahead of Misiorowski (.234). Where Statcast tracks the individual FRVs behind each pitcher, Baseball Reference’s WAR adjustments are at the team level, which may be heavy-handed for pitchers who differ in groundball/fly ball orientation. Sanchez’s 58.2% groundball rate leads the league, while Luzardo’s 48.3% is seventh; both are more dependent upon the team’s shaky infield than its more middling (but still not good) outfield. In the bWAR calculations, there’s about half a run per nine difference between those two (-0.24 for Luzardo, -0.26 for Sánchez) and the other pair (0.24 for Misiorowski, 0.27 for Sale). The latter duo Phillies pair also gets favorable adjustments for pitching in tougher ballparks (which are tracked individually). The adjustments give the two Phillies the higher bWARs, with Sánchez having the edge.
I think the overall choice comes down to Sánchez’s advantage in volume versus Misiorowski’s edge in dominance, and for some voters or otherwise interested observers, that steers it into subjective and/or aesthetic territory. I can understand favoring the guy at the vanguard of extreme velocity — not just because of the raw velo, but also for what he’s done with it in terms of unhittability and sheer brilliance — but I can also appreciate the impulse to reward a throwback, particularly one working under the adverse conditions of being backed by Trea Turner (-16 DRS, -10 FRV) and Alec Bohm (-8 DRS, -5 FRV). Based on their numbers to this point, I’d vote Misiorowski, but I’d hardly blame anyone for choosing Sánchez. Nevertheless, I suspect his second-half fade has probably doomed him to another second-place finish.

He founded the Futility Infielder website (2001), was a columnist for Baseball Prospectus (2005-2012) and a contributing writer for Sports Illustrated (2012-2018). A falta de dos semanas para que termine la temporada regular del 2026, todo parece indicar que los premios Cy Young de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional están prácticamente definidos.
Esto tiene poco que ver con el resto de los candidatos, que conforman un grupo sólido en ambas ligas, y mucho más con los líderes de la carrera. Cam Schlittler, de los Yankees, y Jacob Misiorowski, de los Cerveceros, simplemente les han cerrado la puerta a sus perseguidores. Ambos lanzadores de poder fueron elegidos de manera unánime en sus respectivas ligas por nuestro panel de 32 votantes de MLB.com y MLB Español en nuestra última encuesta del Cy Young del año.
Los expertos emitieron sus votos por quienes creen que se llevarán el galardón, tomando en cuenta no sólo los resultados hasta ahora, sino también cómo esperan que se desarrollen las últimas dos semanas. A los votantes se les pidió ordenar a sus cinco principales candidatos en cada liga, y los lanzadores recibieron puntos en una escala de 5-4-3-2-1: cinco puntos por un voto al primer lugar, cuatro por uno al segundo y así sucesivamente. Estos son los resultados.
A menos que se indique lo contrario, todas las estadísticas incluyen los juegos disputados hasta el domingo.
Schlittler blanqueó a los Mets durante seis innings en el último juego de la Serie del Subway el domingo, reduciendo su efectividad de la temporada a 1.95. No sólo es la mejor marca de la Liga Americana, sino que además está empatado con Misiorowski con la más baja entre los lanzadores calificados de Grandes Ligas. Schlittler ha permitido una carrera o menos en cada una de sus últimas siete aperturas, cerrando con broche de oro su primera temporada completa en las Mayores. Sigue dominando a los bateadores con una combinación de tres tipos de recta, la misma fórmula que utilizó para irrumpir en escena durante la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana en la postemporada pasada. Con octubre a la vuelta de la esquina, otra gran actuación en los playoffs podría estar muy cerca.
Cease ha estado sencillamente brillante en el primer año del contrato de siete temporadas que firmó con los Azulejos en noviembre pasado. Sumó nueve ponches en su apertura más reciente, el domingo ante los Orioles, su 13er juego de la temporada con nueve o más abanicados, más que cualquier otro lanzador de la Liga Americana. Los 236 ponches de Cease representan una nueva marca personal en una campaña y lo tienen empatado con Misiorowski con la mayor cantidad en Grandes Ligas. Este año, Cease ha utilizado un repertorio más equilibrado para complementar su letal combinación de recta de cuatro costuras y slider, dándole distintas maneras de enfrentar a las alineaciones rivales. Ésa es parte de la razón por la que el promedio de bateo de .177 en su contra es el más bajo entre los lanzadores calificados de la Liga Americana.
Quizás no esté al mismo nivel que Schlittler o Cease, pero Messick ha estado indiscutiblemente fantástico en su temporada de novato. El zurdo de peculiar mecánica permitió apenas una carrera en 5.1 innings en su apertura más reciente contra los Mellizos el viernes y, aun en plena lucha por los playoffs, eso es simplemente lo que hace Messick. Schlittler y Cease son los únicos dos lanzadores de la Liga Americana con más presentaciones de cinco o más entradas permitiendo una carrera o menos esta temporada. La efectividad de 2.51 de Messick es la quinta mejor de Grandes Ligas. La recta de cuatro costuras ha sido la clave de su éxito. Aunque Messick no lanza particularmente fuerte, con un promedio de apenas 94.3 mph, su recta de cuatro costuras ha sido uno de los pitcheos individuales más valiosos de Grandes Ligas, según la métrica de valor de carreras de Statcast.
El viernes, los Rays se convirtieron en el primer equipo en asegurar un boleto a la postemporada este año gracias a un dramático jonrón del dominicano Junior Caminero para dejar en el terreno al rival. Pero tampoco hay que olvidar a Rasmussen, quien abrió el juego por Tampa Bay y navegó sin mayores problemas durante siete entradas de una carrera. No debería sorprender que los Rays hayan ganado, porque eso es precisamente lo que hacen cuando Rasmussen sube a la lomita: han ganado cada una de sus últimas 10 aperturas, una racha que se remonta a la pausa del Juego de Estrellas. El derecho de 31 años se ubica entre los cinco mejores de la Liga Americana en efectividad (2.81), WHIP (0.92) y promedio de bateo en contra (.203), apoyándose en tres variantes de recta y un comando impecable.
Boston avanza con paso firme hacia un boleto a la postemporada respaldado por uno de los mejores cuerpos de lanzadores del béisbol. Esa frase habría tenido sentido en el Día Inaugural, pero no si se hubiera sabido que el zurdo Garrett Crochet estaría fuera de acción desde finales de abril. En ausencia de Crochet, Gray ha asumido el papel de as. Tiene marca de 17-5 con efectividad de 2.76 en 27 aperturas y, aunque las victorias de un lanzador no lo son todo, vale la pena destacar que ningún pitcher de la Liga Americana tiene más triunfos que Gray. Busca terminar por tercera vez en su carrera entre los cinco primeros en la votación del Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana: fue segundo con los Mellizos en el 2023 y terminó tercero con los Atléticos en el 2015.
Otros que recibieron votos: Reid Detmers, Angelinos; Gavin Williams, Guardianes; Nick Martínez, Rays; Michael Wacha, Reales
LIGA NACIONAL
El Miz dejó atrás un inusual tropiezo con una sensacional apertura el martes pasado, dominando a los Cachorros durante 6.1 innings de una carrera y nueve ponches. El imponente derecho lidera a los lanzadores de la Liga Nacional en casi todas las categorías estadísticas, incluyendo efectividad (1.95), promedio de bateo en contra (.155) y ponches (236). Incluso con 161.1 entradas a cuestas, Misiorowski sigue lanzando fuego. Ya ha realizado 1,010 pitcheos a 100 mph o más esta temporada, más del doble que el lanzador que le sigue (Mason Miller, 468).
El eterno maravilla ha hecho todo lo posible por cerrar la brecha en la lucha por el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Nacional en la recta final. La efectividad de 2.18 de Sale es la segunda mejor de la Liga Nacional y la más baja para el lanzador de 37 años en una temporada desde el 2018. Ha sido notablemente consistente, permitiendo tres carreras o menos en cada una de sus últimas 23 aperturas. Ningún otro abridor ha tenido una racha de más de 16 juegos consecutivos permitiendo tres anotaciones o menos esta temporada. Sale está desafiando el paso del tiempo gracias, en parte, a una mejor velocidad, lanzando más fuerte que nunca como abridor.
Sánchez cayó un puesto con respecto a nuestra encuesta anterior después de permitir nueve carreras en sus últimas dos aperturas. Aun así, el espigado zurdo dominicano está armando una temporada que merece mucha consideración para el Cy Young. Sánchez ha lanzado la segunda mayor cantidad de innings en el béisbol (187.1), con la quinta mejor efectividad (2.79) y el tercer mejor FIP (2.72) entre los lanzadores calificados de la Liga Nacional. Según la versión de WAR de Baseball Reference, Sánchez ha sido el pitcher más valioso de la Gran Carpa en el 2026, acumulando 7.6 de WAR.
Luzardo se mete en nuestra encuesta final del Cy Young impulsado por una brillante blanqueada contra los Bravos, líderes del Este de la Liga Nacional, en el Día del Trabajo. Ya era hora de que el zurdo peruano-venezolano recibiera el reconocimiento que merece. Luzardo tiene marca de 8-1 con efectividad de 1.66 en sus últimas 12 aperturas, registrando la mejor efectividad de Grandes Ligas desde el 1ro de julio y ganando el premio al Lanzador del Mes de la Liga Nacional en agosto. Respaldado por un letal sweeper que desarrolló la temporada pasada, Luzardo posee la segunda tasa de ponches más alta (30.4%) de la Liga Nacional. Los aficionados de los Filis están a la expectativa después de que Luzardo se perdiera su última apertura debido a una molestia en el hombro, aunque dijo que “no estaba preocupado” tras someterse a una resonancia magnética.
Nos hemos acostumbrado a esperar tanto de Yamamoto que incluso sus mejores actuaciones parecen rutinarias, como su joya de siete entradas y 10 ponches contra los Rojos la noche del miércoles pasado. Sigue siendo el as de una rotación repleta de estrellas digna de Hollywood, con efectividad de 2.62 en 26 aperturas. Pocos lanzadores son mejores que Yamamoto a la hora de mantener corredores fuera de las bases, ya que su WHIP de 0.88 y su promedio de bateo en contra de .184 ocupan el segundo lugar en el Viejo Circuito, sólo por detrás de Misiorowski.
Otros que recibieron votos: Chase Burns, Rojos; el venezolano Eduardo Rodríguez, Diamondbacks; Mason Miller, Padres; Zack Wheeler, Filis

item.content:encoded:
With two weeks to go in the 2026 regular season, it sure looks like the AL and NL Cy Young Awards are all but wrapped up.
This has little to do with the field -- which is strong in both leagues -- and more to do with the frontrunners. The Yankees' Cam Schlittler and the Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski have simply slammed the door shut. Both high-octane hurlers were a unanimous choice in their respective leagues among our panel of 32 MLB.com voters in our final Cy Young poll of the year.
The experts cast their votes for who they think will take home the hardware based not only on the results so far, but also how they expect the final two weeks to shake out. Voters were asked to rank their top five picks in each league, with pitchers receiving points on a 5-4-3-2-1 scale -- five points for a first-place vote, four points for a second-place vote and so on.
Unless otherwise noted, all stats are through play on Sunday.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
Schlittler blanked the Mets across six innings in the Subway Series finale on Sunday, lowering his season ERA to 1.95. Not only is that the best mark in the AL, it's also tied with Misiorowski for the lowest among qualified pitchers in the Majors. Schlittler has now allowed one run or fewer in each of his last seven starts, closing his first full Major League season with a flourish. He continues to overwhelm hitters with a three-fastball combo, the same formula that he used to burst onto the scene in the AL Wild Card Series last postseason. With October looming, an encore is right around the corner.
Cease has been nothing short of brilliant in the first year of a seven-year deal that he signed with the Blue Jays last November. He notched nine strikeouts in his most recent outing on Sunday against the Orioles, his 13th game this season with nine or more strikeouts -- more than any other AL pitcher. Cease's 236 strikeouts are a new single-season high and tied with Misiorowski for the most in the Majors. This year, Cease has used a more balanced pitch mix to supplement his lethal four-seam fastball/slider combo, giving him different ways to navigate opposing lineups. It's part of the reason why Cease's .177 batting average against is lowest among qualified AL pitchers.
He may not be on the same level as Schlittler or Cease, but Messick has been undeniably fantastic in his rookie season. The funky left-hander allowed just one run in 5 1/3 innings in his last start against the Twins on Friday and, even in the heat of the pennant race, that is simply what Messick does. Schlittler and Cease are the only two AL pitchers to have more outings of five or more innings while allowing one run or fewer this season. Messick's 2.51 ERA is fifth best in the Majors. The four-seam fastball is the key to his success. Though Messick doesn't throw hard -- sitting just 94.3 mph -- his four-seamer has been one of the most valuable individual pitches in the Majors, according to Statcast's run value metric.
On Friday, the Rays became the first team to clinch a postseason berth this year thanks to a dramatic walk-off home run from Junior Caminero. Not to be forgotten, Rasmussen started the game for Tampa Bay and breezed through seven innings of one-run ball. It shouldn't be a surprise that the Rays won because that is what they do when Rasmussen is on the hill: They have won each of his last 10 starts, a stretch that dates back to the All-Star break. The 31-year-old right-hander ranks in the top five in the AL in ERA (2.81), WHIP (0.92) and batting average against (.203), relying on three fastball shapes and impeccable command.
Boston is coasting toward a postseason berth behind one of baseball's best pitching staffs. That sentence would have made sense on Opening Day, but not if you knew that left-hander Garrett Crochet would be sidelined since late April. In Crochet's absence, Gray has stepped up as the ace. He is 17-5 with a 2.76 ERA in 27 starts, and while pitcher wins aren't everything, it's noteworthy that no AL pitcher has more wins than Gray. He is vying for his third career top-five finish in AL Cy Young Award voting: He was the runner up with the Twins in 2023 and finished No. 3 with the Athletics in 2015.
Others receiving votes: Reid Detmers, Angels; Gavin Williams, Guardians; Nick Martinez, Rays; Michael Wacha, Royals
NATIONAL LEAGUE
The Miz put a rare blip behind him with a sensational start last Tuesday, stifling the Cubs over 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball with nine strikeouts. The overpowering righty leads NL pitchers in nearly every statistical category, including ERA (1.95), batting average against (.155) and K's (236). Even with 161 1/3 innings under his belt, Misiorowski continues to bring the heat, too. He has now thrown 1,010 pitches at 100 mph or harder this season, more than double the next closest pitcher (Mason Miller, 468).
The ageless wonder has tried his best to close the gap in the NL Cy Young Award race down the stretch. Sale's 2.18 ERA is the second best in the NL and the lowest by the 37-year-old in a single season since 2018. He's been remarkably consistent, allowing three runs or fewer in each of his last 23 starts. No other starting pitcher has a stretch of more than 16 consecutive games allowing three runs or fewer this season. Sale is defying Father Time thanks in part to improved velocity, throwing harder than he ever has as a starting pitcher.
Sánchez dropped a spot from our previous poll after allowing nine runs across his last two starts. Still, the lanky left-hander is putting together a season that merits plenty of Cy Young consideration. Sánchez has pitched the second-most innings in baseball (187 1/3) with the fifth best ERA (2.79) and third best FIP (2.72) among qualified NL pitchers. By Baseball Reference's version of WAR, Sánchez has been the most valuable pitcher in baseball in 2026, tallying 7.6 WAR.
Luzardo cracks our final Cy Young poll on the backs of a brilliant shutout against the NL East-leading Braves on Labor Day. It's well past time that the left-hander receives his flowers. Luzardo is 8-1 with a 1.66 ERA in his last 12 starts, posting the lowest ERA in the Majors since July 1 and winning the NL Pitcher of the Month Award in August. Buoyed by a lethal sweeper that he developed last season, Luzardo has the second-highest strikeout rate (30.4%) in the National League. Phillies fans are holding their breath after Luzardo missed his last start due to a shoulder ailment, though he said he was "not concerned" following his MRI.
We have come to expect so much of Yamamoto that even his best performances feel routine -- like his seven-inning, 10-strikeout gem against the Reds last Wednesday. He is still the ace of a star-studded rotation befitting Hollywood, with a 2.62 ERA through 26 starts. Few pitchers are better at limiting traffic than Yamamoto, whose 0.88 WHIP and .184 batting average against are each second in the NL behind Misiorowski.
Others receiving votes: Chase Burns, Reds; Eduardo Rodriguez, D-backs; Mason Miller, Padres; Zack Wheeler, Phillies

The American League East has always been the sport's most star-driven division, even when the standings don't always show it. The New York Yankees-Boston Red Sox rivalry alone has produced decades of this, but it's not just those two anymore.
The Toronto Blue Jays have peaked into a real contender, the Tampa Bay Rays are leading this year's race and continue to develop, and the Baltimore Orioles are always one prospect wave away from popping off again. With that much noise in one division, it's easy to lose track of just how much individual talent is walking around it.
Case in point: with Tarik Skubal now pitching for the Los Angeles Dodgers, this year's AL Cy Young race is shaping up to be a battle between two AL East arms, Cam Schlittler and Dylan Cease. That trophy is staying in this division no matter what. But for Red Sox fans, it's worth saying the obvious: if Garrett Crochet had stayed healthy all year, he'd be right in that conversation too, not watching it from the outside looking in.
A healthy Garrett Crochet would've made the 2026 AL Cy Young Award race more interesting
It's easy to forget just how dominant Crochet was in 2025. He went 18-5 with a 2.59 ERA across a league-leading 205.1 innings, struck out a league-best 255 batters, and finished as the AL Cy Young runner-up behind Skubal himself. Take a quick glance at his Baseball Savant page from that season and it reads like a cheat code, elite percentile marks across nearly every meaningful category a pitcher can be graded on. That's the version of Crochet the division rivals were supposed to get again in 2026.
Instead, he was clearly not right from the start, posting an ugly-looking 6.30 ERA across his first six starts before landing on the injured list on April 29 with a shoulder issue that turned into a lat problem after a setback in May. The strikeouts were still there (37 in just 30 innings), but the results were far from pretty, and Boston has been without its ace for basically the entire season since.
Here's where it gets exciting again, though. Crochet threw a bullpen session at Fenway this week, his second since resuming throwing, and interim manager Chad Tracy has been candid that a return this season likely means relief work, not a return to the rotation. Crochet has relief experience already from earlier in his career, and has shown flashes of pure domincance. In 72 bullpen appearances, he logged 73 innings with 85 punchies and 2.71 ERA. In his four postseason relief outings, he has a 0.00 ERA and has struck out 6 of the 14 batters he faced.
He's also made it clear he has zero ego about the role. With Boston fighting to hold onto that second Wild Card spot, a healthy Crochet coming out of the bullpen in high-leverage October moments would be about as fun a development as this fanbase could ask for down the stretch.
